title: Investor Renovation Contractor in Houston, TX | Genstone
metaDescription: Houston investor rehabs priced before you offer: pier-and-beam leveling, slab plumbing, flood history and Permitting Center sign-offs, with draws tied to work.
intro: Houston rewards investors who read the dirt and the flood maps before they read the comps. A bungalow in the Heights, a slab ranch in Sharpstown and a raised cottage in Fifth Ward can sit at similar purchase prices and need completely different scopes, because Gulf Coast clay, a long history of flooding and decades of humid heat leave very different marks on each. Genstone Construction plans and manages renovations for investors, lenders and servicers across the city by coordinating vetted, licensed contractors who work in Houston every day, while our estimators, field managers and billing team keep the job organized from our Romeoville, Illinois headquarters. Before you commit capital, our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the repairs, pressure-tests your after-repair value and tells you whether the deal still works once foundation, drain line and drainage questions are answered. After closing you get a detailed scope with a draw schedule, one field manager, permits handled through the city, and progress you can follow without driving out to the property.
housingStock:
Houston grew outward in waves, and each ring of the city carries the building habits of its decade. The oldest inner neighborhoods, including the Heights, Woodland Heights, Third Ward, Fifth Ward, Eastwood and parts of Montrose, are full of early twentieth-century frame bungalows, Craftsman cottages and a handful of shotgun houses, almost all of them on pier-and-beam foundations. Those crawlspaces are a gift and a liability. They give your plumber and electrician access without cutting concrete, but decades of shifting clay leave sagging floors, rotted sill plates and cedar or concrete piers that have tilted or sunk.

After World War II the city filled in with slab-on-grade ranches. Oak Forest, Garden Oaks, Spring Branch, Sharpstown, Meyerland and Westbury are dominated by brick-veneer homes from the 1950s through the 1970s. Their weak point is underneath: original cast-iron drain lines running through the slab, which crack and belly as the soil moves, and supply lines that may be galvanized steel in the earliest examples. A hydrostatic test and a camera run are routine diligence on these houses, not extras.

The 1970s and 1980s brought larger subdivisions in Alief, the Energy Corridor and the northern suburbs, along with materials of that era such as aluminum branch wiring in some homes, polybutylene supply lines in some later builds and early composite siding that swells when wet. More recently, inner-loop lots have been carved into three-story townhomes, which matters to investors mostly as comps: a small renovated bungalow now competes against new construction on the same block. Across every era, the common thread is moisture. Houston houses fail from water in the soil, water in the air and water coming in from the street, and a good rehab budget is built around stopping all three.

commonIssues.title: Foundation movement on expansive clay
commonIssues.body: Much of Houston sits on clay that swells when wet and shrinks in drought, so slabs crack and pier-and-beam floors drift out of level. On a slab ranch we look for stair-step cracks in brick, doors that stick, and gaps at window frames. On a bungalow we crawl the space to check piers, beams and shims. Either way, the repair scope and the engineer's letter need to be settled before cosmetic work begins, because buyers, appraisers and lenders all ask about it.

commonIssues.title: Cast-iron drains under the slab
commonIssues.body: Postwar homes in Oak Forest, Meyerland, Sharpstown and similar neighborhoods frequently still have original cast-iron sewer lines beneath the concrete. Soil movement and age leave them cracked, scaled or sagging, and the first sign is often a slow drain or a sewer smell after move-in. A camera inspection before you buy shows if the house needs a spot repair, a tunnel under the slab or a full reroute through the attic and walls, and those are very different line items.

commonIssues.title: Flood history and hidden water damage
commonIssues.body: Large parts of the city took water during Hurricane Harvey, the Tax Day and Memorial Day floods, and Tropical Storm Allison before them. Some houses were gutted and rebuilt properly, others were patched. We check for replaced drywall at a consistent height, swollen baseboards, rusted outlet boxes and musty wall cavities. Prior flooding affects insurance, buyer appetite and, in mapped floodplains, how much renovation the city allows before raising the house becomes part of the conversation.

commonIssues.title: Humidity, mold and attic heat
commonIssues.body: Houston's long, sticky summers punish houses with leaky ductwork, undersized or aging air conditioning and poor attic ventilation. Condensation on uninsulated ducts drips into ceilings, bath fans that vent into the attic feed mold, and closed-up vacant homes grow it on every surface. Our scopes usually include duct sealing or replacement, proper exhaust venting, and a correctly sized system, because a house that cannot hold humidity down will not stay rented or sold.

commonIssues.title: Termites and wood rot
commonIssues.body: Warm, wet conditions make Houston prime territory for subterranean termites, including the Formosan species that has established itself along the Gulf Coast. Pier-and-beam houses are especially exposed where wood siding or framing sits close to soil. We look at sill plates, rim joists, door jambs and the bottom courses of siding, and we budget for treatment plus replacement of damaged members rather than painting over soft wood that will fail a buyer's inspection.

investorMarket:
Houston is large enough that it behaves like several markets at once, and strategy should follow the submarket rather than the city average.

Inside the loop, the Heights, Woodland Heights, Montrose and the East End are where fix-and-flip margins come from cosmetic and systems work on character bungalows. Buyers there want original details kept and everything behind the walls replaced, and they compare your finished house against new townhomes, so finish selection matters more than in the suburbs. Historic district rules in parts of the Heights also limit what you can change on the street side.

The postwar slab ranches of Oak Forest, Garden Oaks and Spring Branch support both flips and long-term holds. These are solid houses with good lots, and the scope tends to center on drain lines, electrical updates, kitchens and baths. Areas such as Sharpstown, Alief, Greenspoint and the northeast side lean toward buy-and-hold and BRRRR, where purchase prices leave room for a full systems rehab and rental demand is steady from households working across the region's medical, energy and port economies.

Near Northside, Kashmere Gardens, Sunnyside and Acres Homes see a mix of rental investors, small builders and REO activity. Here the deciding factors are flood exposure, foundation condition and whether the lot is worth more than the house. A Pre-Offer Rehab Review is especially useful in these areas, because the gap between a cosmetic turn and a structural rebuild can be hard to see from the curb.
permits:
Inside city limits, residential building permits are issued through the Houston Permitting Center, part of Houston Public Works. Structural repairs, foundation work, new or relocated plumbing, electrical service and circuit work, HVAC replacement, roofing in many cases, window and door openings that change framing, and additions all require permits and inspections. Plumbing, electrical and mechanical work must be pulled by trades licensed through the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners or the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

Two local rules change rehab plans more than any others. First, Houston has no conventional zoning, but deed restrictions are enforced by civic associations and the city, so allowable use and exterior changes are often controlled at the subdivision level. Second, the city's floodplain ordinance applies a substantial-improvement test to work on homes in mapped flood hazard areas: if renovation or repair cost crosses the threshold relative to the structure's value, the house may have to be raised or otherwise brought into compliance. We check floodplain status and prior damage before scoping. Properties in designated historic districts, including several in the Heights, also need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Houston Archaeological and Historical Commission for exterior changes. Unincorporated addresses fall under Harris County's permitting office instead.
climate:
Houston's climate shapes both what goes into a rehab and when it happens. From late spring through early fall, heat and humidity slow exterior painting, roofing and concrete work, and interior drywall and flooring need the air conditioning running to cure and acclimate properly. Afternoon storms interrupt roof tear-offs, so roofers schedule around the radar.

Hurricane season runs through the summer and fall, and a named storm near the coast can pause work, flood a site or pull every roofer in the region onto insurance jobs. Winter is short and mild, which makes it the most productive stretch for exterior work, but Winter Storm Uri in 2021 showed that hard freezes do happen. Pipes in exterior walls and attics burst across the city, and vacant homes were hit hardest. We now treat freeze protection as part of scoping, especially for plumbing runs in uninsulated spaces.

faqs.q: Do you work in Houston suburbs like Pasadena, Pearland and Katy?
faqs.a: Yes. We coordinate licensed contractors across the Houston metro, including Pasadena, Pearland, Sugar Land, Katy, Baytown, Humble and Spring. Each of those cities runs its own building department and, in some cases, its own floodplain rules, and unincorporated areas fall under Harris County or the neighboring county. We confirm which office has jurisdiction before scoping so the permit plan matches the address rather than assuming City of Houston rules apply everywhere.

faqs.q: Can you renovate a house that flooded during Harvey?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, but the order of operations matters. We start by confirming whether the home is in a mapped floodplain and whether the earlier repairs were permitted. If the cost of the work you want approaches the city's substantial-improvement threshold, raising the structure or other compliance work may come into play. We also open suspect walls to check for remaining moisture and mold. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review lays those questions out before you commit to the purchase.

faqs.q: How do you handle foundation repair on a Houston flip?
faqs.a: We bring in a licensed foundation contractor and, where the scope calls for it, a structural engineer to evaluate and document the repair. The engineer's letter and any transferable warranty from the foundation company become part of your sale or refinance package. Foundation work goes first in the schedule, because leveling a house cracks drywall, moves door frames and can affect plumbing, and you do not want to redo finishes that were installed too early.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay upfront?
faqs.a: No. Genstone does not collect an upfront payment. Construction draws are tied to completed work that you can verify through photos and milestone documentation, and final payment comes after completion and your approval. Dumpster and debris costs are already included in our estimates, so you are not surprised by haul-off charges on a gut job. Our work carries a one-year workmanship warranty, which does not cover tenant damage or normal wear.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Houston, TX | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Houston fix and flip renovations scoped against Heights townhome comps and slab-ranch buyers: drain lines, leveling, finishes and draws tied to finished work.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Houston
fix-flip.intro: A Houston flip is won or lost on two questions: what is wrong underneath the house, and who is the buyer on that street. In the Heights and the East End, your bungalow sells next to new three-story townhomes, so buyers expect the charm of an old house with the systems of a new one. In Oak Forest or Spring Branch, the buyer is comparing your slab ranch against other updated ranches and will send an inspector straight to the drain lines and the foundation. Genstone builds flip scopes around those realities. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the work and checks your ARV before you commit, and after closing a single field manager runs a coordinated crew of licensed local contractors so the house reaches the market with the paperwork that Houston buyers and their inspectors ask for.

sections.h2: Spend where Houston buyers and inspectors look first
sections.body:
Most Houston buyers hire an inspector who will run a hydrostatic test on a slab house or crawl a pier-and-beam house, and the report shapes the renegotiation. That means the money you put into the hidden parts of the house protects your sale price as much as the kitchen does. On a 1950s or 1960s ranch, our scopes usually start with a camera run of the cast-iron drains and a decision on replacing them. On a bungalow, we level the floor system, replace rotted sill plates and correct the piers before anyone hangs drywall.

After that, the visible spend follows the street. In the Heights and Woodland Heights, buyers pay for refinished original pine floors, restored windows or quality replacements that suit the house, period-appropriate trim and a kitchen that feels current without looking like a townhome interior. In Garden Oaks and Oak Forest, open sightlines between kitchen and living room, updated baths and a clean exterior matter more than historic detail. We give you more than one finish level in the estimate so you can match the comps instead of guessing.

sections.h2: Keeping carrying costs down in a humid, storm-prone city
sections.body:
Every month a flip sits unfinished adds interest, insurance and utility costs, and Houston adds weather to the list. We sequence the work so the house is dried in and the air conditioning is running early. That protects new drywall, flooring and cabinets from humidity, which can cause cupping and swelling if materials go in before the house is conditioned. Roofing and exterior work are scheduled around storm patterns, and during hurricane season we plan for the possibility that roofers get pulled onto insurance claims after a named storm.

Permits are the other schedule driver. Foundation repair, plumbing reroutes, electrical panel upgrades and HVAC replacement all go through the Houston Permitting Center, and inspections have to pass in order. Our field manager stacks inspections so trades are not standing around waiting. Because draws are tied to completed work, you see progress before money moves, and the milestone photos give you something concrete to share with your lender or partners.

sections.h2: Flood maps, deed restrictions and historic rules before you buy
sections.body:
Some Houston flips run into trouble that has nothing to do with construction. If the house is in a mapped floodplain, a large renovation can trigger the city's substantial-improvement rules and turn a cosmetic flip into a project that requires raising the house or other floodproofing work. Prior flood claims also affect your buyer's insurance quote, which shrinks or grows your buyer pool. We look at floodplain status, drainage on the block and visible signs of past water before the Pre-Offer Rehab Review is final.

Deed restrictions matter too. Houston does not have traditional zoning, but many subdivisions in Garden Oaks, Oak Forest, Meyerland and elsewhere carry restrictions on setbacks, additions, fences and exterior materials, and civic associations do enforce them. In the Heights historic districts, the Houston Archaeological and Historical Commission reviews exterior changes, and a planned window swap, siding replacement or porch rebuild may need a Certificate of Appropriateness. Knowing those constraints up front keeps your scope realistic, keeps your listing photos honest and keeps the closing on schedule.

faqs.q: Should I keep the original windows on a Heights bungalow flip?
faqs.a: It depends on condition and whether the house sits in a historic district. Restored wood windows are often what Heights buyers want, and replacement on the street side may require review by the Houston Archaeological and Historical Commission. If the sashes are rotted beyond repair, a quality wood or clad replacement that matches the original profile is the usual compromise. We price both paths so you can compare cost against what the comps reward.

faqs.q: Do you replace cast-iron drains on every slab ranch flip?
faqs.a: Not automatically. We recommend a camera inspection first. If the lines are intact and draining well, spot repairs may be enough. If they are scaled, cracked or bellied, replacement now usually costs less than renegotiating with a buyer whose inspector finds the problem. Replacement can mean tunneling under the slab or rerouting through the walls and attic, and we price whichever method suits the house.

faqs.q: Can I list during hurricane season?
faqs.a: Yes, and many Houston flips do. The practical concern is your schedule rather than the sale. A storm can delay roofing and exterior work and tighten trade availability, so we build some flexibility into the plan and get the house dried in early. Buyers will also ask about flood history and drainage, so having documentation of the work you did ready for the listing helps.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Houston, TX | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR rehabs in Houston built for the refinance appraisal and the tenant: slab plumbing, durable finishes, efficient AC and paperwork your lender will review.
brrrr.intro: BRRRR in Houston works best on the houses that flippers overlook: brick slab ranches in Sharpstown, Alief and the north side, and older frame homes in the East End and Northside that need a full systems update before they can rent. The rehab has two jobs. It has to support the appraised value your refinance depends on, and it has to stand up to tenants and Gulf Coast humidity for years without constant service calls. Genstone scopes BRRRR projects around both. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the work and estimates the ARV before you buy, and Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans if you want to line up the refinance alongside the renovation. During construction, one field manager coordinates licensed local contractors, permits and inspections, and you get documented progress that is useful for both your lender and your records.

sections.body:
Houston appraisers lean on recent comparable sales within a tight radius, and they look for evidence that the house is fully functional and free of major deferred maintenance. For BRRRR, that means the big-ticket items need to be visibly addressed: roof, foundation, drain lines, electrical panel, water heater and air conditioning. A Sharpstown ranch with new finishes but an original panel and a failing AC unit will appraise below one with modest finishes and fully updated systems.

We help you target the finish level the comps support rather than overbuilding. In much of southwest and north Houston, comparable rentals and sales have durable vinyl plank, solid-surface or quartz counters and updated fixtures, not high-end tile work. Spending beyond that rarely moves the appraisal. What does move it is square footage that counts, so if a previous owner enclosed a garage without permits, we discuss whether to permit it properly or return it to garage use. Keeping permit records and the foundation engineer's letter organized also helps when the appraiser or underwriter asks.

sections.h2: Materials that survive tenants and Gulf Coast humidity
sections.body:
A rental in Houston has to cope with long cooling seasons, sticky indoor air when the system is undersized, and the occasional water event from a storm or a failed supply line. We specify finishes that hold up to that. Luxury vinyl plank instead of laminate, because laminate swells when it gets wet. Semi-gloss paint in kitchens and baths. Cement board behind tile. Properly ducted bath exhaust fans that vent outside, not into the attic where they feed mold on the roof decking.

The air conditioning system matters more here than in most markets. An undersized or poorly installed system runs constantly, fails to pull moisture out of the air, and generates tenant calls and mold complaints by August. We size equipment to the house, seal or replace leaky attic ductwork, and make sure condensate lines and pans drain properly with a float switch. For pier-and-beam rentals in the East End or Northside, we look at crawlspace ventilation and vapor control so floors do not cup. These choices keep turnover costs down and help the property hold its value when it is time to reappraise or sell.

sections.h2: Neighborhoods and houses that fit the BRRRR model
sections.body:
The Houston houses that make BRRRR math work are usually ones with good bones and obvious deferred maintenance. Brick ranches in Sharpstown, Alief, Greenspoint and around Aldine often fit, because the brick shell holds up well and the scope concentrates on interior systems, drains and finishes. Frame houses in Eastwood, Magnolia Park and Second Ward can work as well, though wood siding, termite damage and pier-and-beam leveling add scope that has to be priced honestly.

We are cautious about properties with repeated flood history or significant foundation movement unless the price clearly reflects it. Those issues can limit your refinance options, raise flood and hazard insurance costs and slow your lease-up, and a lender ordering the refinance appraisal will see the same water lines on the drywall that you did. During the Pre-Offer Rehab Review, we check floodplain status, look for signs of past water and assess the foundation so you can see whether the property supports a refinance before you commit capital. Sometimes the right answer is to pass, and we will tell you that.

faqs.q: Can Genstone Financial refinance my Houston BRRRR property?
faqs.a: Genstone Financial offers DSCR rental loans, fix-and-flip loans, lines of credit and new construction loans. A DSCR loan qualifies based on the property's rental income rather than your personal income, which suits many BRRRR investors holding several Houston rentals. Using Genstone Financial is optional. We provide the same scope, draw documentation, permit records and completion photos to any lender you choose.

faqs.q: What causes a Houston BRRRR appraisal to come in low?
faqs.a: The usual causes are unaddressed systems, unpermitted garage conversions, weak comps and visible signs of foundation or water problems. An appraiser who sees stair-step cracks in brick, an original panel or a failing condenser will adjust downward. We address those items in the scope and keep permit records and engineer letters ready so you can answer underwriting questions quickly. Pulling a few recent renovated sales from the same subdivision before you set your finish level also keeps expectations honest.

faqs.q: Do you handle tenant-ready make-ready after the rehab?
faqs.a: Yes. The final phase of a BRRRR scope includes a make-ready punch list: deep clean, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors where required, rekeyed locks, blinds, a fresh AC filter and a final walkthrough. Genstone Property Management and Field Services can also support leasing and ongoing maintenance on your Houston rental if you want help after the renovation, so the same team that built the scope can answer the first tenant call.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Houston, TX | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Single-family rental rehabs across Houston with portfolio-wide standards: humidity-ready finishes, AC and drain-line fixes, permits and documented draws.
rental-renovation.intro: Houston has one of the country's largest single-family rental markets, and much of that inventory is brick slab ranches and suburban tract homes from the 1970s onward. Keeping those houses rentable means repeating the same disciplined scope across many addresses: dependable air conditioning, sound plumbing, durable floors and finishes that survive Gulf Coast humidity and frequent turnover. Genstone works with individual landlords, funds and institutional owners on rental renovations in Houston and the surrounding suburbs. We coordinate licensed local contractors, set consistent material standards across the portfolio, and give you one field manager per project plus a clear draw schedule. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps acquisitions teams price houses before they buy, and the scope documents we produce make it easier to compare properties and track spending.

sections.h2: A rental standard built for Houston conditions
sections.body:
Portfolio owners in Houston do best with a written finish and systems standard that every rehab follows. Ours is built around the problems that generate the most tenant calls here. Air conditioning comes first: properly sized equipment, sealed ductwork, clean condensate drainage and a programmable thermostat. Plumbing comes next, with special attention to slab drain lines, water heater placement in garages and attics, and supply line materials in older homes.

For finishes, we standardize on waterproof vinyl plank, durable paint colors that can be touched up easily, solid cabinet boxes and hardware that can be replaced without special ordering. Bathrooms get exhaust fans vented outside and tile or one-piece surrounds that resist mold. Exterior work focuses on drainage, gutters and keeping soil graded away from slabs and crawlspaces, because water pooling against the foundation in a Houston downpour is the root of many repair calls. A consistent standard keeps per-unit costs predictable and makes future turns faster.

sections.h2: Scaling across Harris County and the suburbs
sections.body:
Rental portfolios in Houston rarely sit in one neighborhood. An owner might hold slab ranches in Alief, newer tract homes in Katy and Cypress, and older houses in Pasadena or Channelview. Each area has its own building department, and a lot of rental inventory sits in unincorporated Harris County inside municipal utility districts, where permitting and floodplain review follow county rules rather than City of Houston rules. A portfolio approach needs that local knowledge layered on top of a shared standard.

Genstone's network of licensed, insured contractors lets us cover a wide footprint while keeping scope language and pricing consistent. Each project gets one field manager who handles permits, inspections, lien waivers and contractor compliance. You see progress and milestones through documentation instead of site visits, which matters when you are managing many addresses across a metro this spread out. Our estimators also flag houses that need more than a standard turn, such as foundation movement, a roof at the end of its life or a cast-iron drain line that is failing, so capital planning reflects the real condition of each asset.

sections.h2: Turnover and preventive work between tenants
sections.body:
In Houston, the best time to fix a recurring problem is between tenants. A turn is a chance to replace a water heater before it leaks through a ceiling, service the condenser and coil before the summer load arrives, re-caulk tubs, clear gutters and check the attic for roof leaks, rodent entry and poor ventilation. We scope turns to catch those items rather than repainting and moving on.

Timing helps too. A turn that lands in late spring is the right moment for AC work, because once the heat sets in, HVAC contractors across the city are booked solid with emergency calls. A turn in fall or winter is a good time for roof and exterior repairs, before the next hurricane season. Genstone Field Services also handles occupied maintenance, inspections and code compliance, so the same organization can support your properties between renovations. Our one-year workmanship warranty applies to the work we perform, excluding tenant damage and normal wear.

faqs.q: Do you work on rentals in unincorporated Harris County?
faqs.a: Yes. A large share of Houston-area rental homes sit in unincorporated areas or in municipal utility districts outside city limits, especially toward Cypress, Spring, Katy and the northeast. Permits there typically go through Harris County rather than the City of Houston, and floodplain review follows county rules. We confirm jurisdiction for each address before scoping so the permit plan is right from the start.

faqs.q: Can you standardize finishes across my whole Houston portfolio?
faqs.a: Yes. We work from a written finish and systems standard that you approve, covering flooring, paint, fixtures, cabinets and HVAC specifications. That keeps costs predictable, simplifies future repairs and makes your homes look consistent to tenants and property managers. We adjust where a specific property's age or condition calls for something different, such as a pier-and-beam house in the East End.

faqs.q: How do you handle rentals with past flood damage?
faqs.a: We inspect for remaining moisture, mold and damaged materials, confirm whether earlier repairs were permitted, and check floodplain status. If the house needs significant repair, we explain how city or county substantial-improvement rules could apply. Clear documentation of what was removed, dried and replaced helps with insurance, tenant questions and an eventual sale. We also look at lot drainage and gutters so the next heavy rain does not repeat the problem.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & Fourplex Renovation in Houston, TX | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Houston 2–4 unit renovations: Montrose fourplexes, Heights garage apartments and East End duplexes, with phased occupied work and shared-system upgrades.
multifamily-renovation.intro: Houston's small multifamily stock is scattered and varied. Montrose and the Museum District have mid-century two-story fourplexes and brick garden-style buildings. The Heights, Woodland Heights and the East End have duplexes, converted bungalows and garage apartments behind the main house. Near the Medical Center and universities, small buildings rent to students and hospital workers. Each type comes with its own shared systems, access issues and code questions. Genstone helps investors renovate duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes across Houston by coordinating licensed local contractors who understand older multifamily construction. We plan work around occupied units, upgrade shared plumbing, electrical and HVAC, and manage permits and inspections. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the property before you buy so you can see whether the rents support the renovation.

sections.h2: What Houston's 2–4 unit buildings tend to need
sections.body:
Many of Houston's small multifamily buildings date from the 1940s through the 1970s, and they share predictable weaknesses. Fourplexes in Montrose and Neartown often have original electrical service sized for window units, not central air, so tenants run portable AC units on overloaded circuits. Plumbing may be galvanized supply with cast-iron drains, and shared drain stacks mean a clog or break affects several units.

Duplexes and converted bungalows in the Heights and East End usually sit on pier-and-beam foundations that need leveling, and interior walls added during conversion may not meet current fire separation expectations. Garage apartments behind single-family homes are common in older neighborhoods, and their legal status varies. Some were permitted, some were built informally decades ago. We review each building's history so you understand what you are buying, then scope electrical service upgrades, separate metering where practical, plumbing replacement and HVAC that matches the unit layout, whether that means split systems per unit or a shared attic plan.

sections.h2: Renovating around tenants in a Houston summer
sections.body:
Buying a Houston fourplex with tenants in some units is common, and vacating the whole building is rarely practical. We phase work so vacant units are renovated first, then occupied units are completed as leases turn or tenants are relocated within the building. Shared-system work, like replacing a main drain, re-piping a building or upgrading the electrical service, is scheduled with written advance notice and short, planned shutoffs.

In a Houston summer, losing air conditioning is more than an inconvenience for an older tenant or a family with a newborn, so HVAC replacement in occupied units is planned for the cooler months whenever possible, or done quickly with temporary cooling on hand. Attic work on two-story fourplexes is also safer and faster outside of peak heat. Our field manager coordinates access, keeps stairways and common areas safe and clean, and documents progress so you can share updates with tenants. Genstone Field Services can also handle occupied maintenance for units not yet renovated, so the building stays in good order throughout the project and you are not juggling a separate handyman.

sections.h2: Permits, deed restrictions and use questions
sections.body:
Because Houston lacks conventional zoning, the question of how many units a lot can legally hold often comes down to deed restrictions and city development rules rather than a zoning map. Some older subdivisions restrict lots to single-family use, which can affect duplexes and garage apartments, while other inner-loop areas have no active restrictions at all. Before you buy, we recommend confirming the restrictions recorded on the lot and whether existing units were ever permitted.

Renovation work on multifamily buildings goes through the Houston Permitting Center, and the city's fire and life-safety requirements for multi-unit residential buildings can come into play, especially for smoke detection, egress windows, stair handrails and separation between units. Off-street parking can also come up if you change the number of units. Structures in the Heights or other historic districts need approval for exterior changes. We map out permit requirements during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so the scope and budget account for compliance from day one instead of after an inspector writes it up.

faqs.q: Can you add separate electric meters to a Houston fourplex?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Separate metering involves upgrading the service, adding a meter bank and running new feeders to each unit, coordinated with CenterPoint Energy and the city's electrical inspection. It can shift utility costs to tenants and improve your operating numbers. We evaluate feasibility on each building, including panel locations and wall access, and include it as an option in the scope.

faqs.q: Is a garage apartment in the Heights a legal rental unit?
faqs.a: It depends on when and how it was built, the deed restrictions on the lot and whether it was ever permitted. Some were built legally decades ago, while others were added informally by a past owner. We review available records and physical conditions and explain what it would take to bring the unit into compliance, so you can price that work before closing.

faqs.q: How do you protect tenants during a Houston multifamily renovation?
faqs.a: We schedule shared shutoffs in advance, keep common areas clear and safe, contain dust and debris, and plan HVAC and attic work for cooler months when possible. Our field manager is the single point of contact for coordination, and progress is documented so you can keep tenants informed about what is happening and when. Most problems with occupied jobs come from surprises, so we try hard not to create any.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Houston, TX | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor for Houston buyers and lenders: foundation, drain line and AC repairs scoped for Limited or Standard loans, with draw support.
fha-203k.intro: An FHA 203(k) loan lets a Houston buyer finance the purchase and the repairs together, which opens up houses that would not pass a standard FHA appraisal. That matters here, because many affordable listings in Houston have exactly the issues that stop conventional financing: foundation movement, failing drain lines, outdated electrical panels, old roofs and air conditioning near the end of its life. Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor. We work with buyers, agents, lenders and HUD consultants to produce the detailed bid, labor and material breakdown and draw schedule the program requires, and we coordinate licensed Houston contractors to complete the work. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review can help a buyer understand repair costs before writing an offer, which keeps the deal realistic from the start.

sections.h2: Limited or Standard on a Houston house
sections.body:
The Limited 203(k) covers non-structural repairs up to the program's $75,000 cap and works well for Houston homes that need updates rather than structural work: a new roof, HVAC replacement, water heater, flooring, kitchen and bath updates, paint and electrical upgrades. Many brick slab ranches in Sharpstown, Westbury and the north side fit this profile once the foundation and drains check out.

The Standard 203(k) is required when the scope includes structural repairs, and in Houston that most often means foundation work. Leveling a pier-and-beam bungalow, installing pressed piers under a cracked slab or replacing a large section of rotted floor framing all push the project into Standard territory. Tunneling under a slab to replace a collapsed drain line can as well, depending on how the work is scoped. The Standard program requires a minimum of $5,000 in repairs and a HUD consultant who inspects the property, prepares the work write-up and approves draws. We coordinate closely with the consultant so the scope, our bid and the draw schedule match line for line.

sections.h2: Houses in Houston that fit a 203(k)
sections.body:
The best Houston candidates are solid houses priced down by obvious, fixable problems. A 1960s brick ranch in Oak Forest with a failing AC, an original panel and a dated kitchen is a classic Limited project. A 1920s bungalow in Eastwood or Lindale Park that needs leveling, rewiring and new plumbing is a natural Standard project, and buyers often end up in a close-in neighborhood they could not otherwise afford.

Flood history is the main caution. A house in a mapped floodplain may face substantial-improvement rules if the renovation is large relative to the structure's value, and the lender will require flood insurance in special flood hazard areas, which changes the buyer's monthly payment. We check floodplain status early so buyers and agents are not surprised at underwriting. Unpermitted additions and garage conversions are another common Houston issue, because the appraiser and the lender want the finished house to be legal and safe. We note those in the bid so they can be permitted or corrected as part of the loan.

sections.h2: Bids, draws and timing on a 203(k)
sections.body:
FHA 203(k) projects run on paperwork. The lender needs a detailed contractor bid that breaks out labor and materials by line item, matching the consultant's write-up on a Standard loan. Draws are released as work is completed and inspected, and the program limits how much can be paid before inspection. Projects above the $15,000 threshold involve additional inspection and documentation requirements.

Genstone's estimators produce bids in the format lenders and consultants expect, and our field manager coordinates draw inspections with the consultant or lender. Because we do not ask for upfront payment and tie draws to completed work, our process lines up with how the program releases funds. In Houston, scheduling also matters for the buyer: many purchasers are paying rent elsewhere while the work happens, so we plan around permit timing at the Houston Permitting Center and order long-lead items like HVAC equipment early. For buyers, that means fewer surprises. For lenders and agents, it means a contractor who understands the documentation the loan requires.

faqs.q: Can a 203(k) cover foundation repair in Houston?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Standard 203(k). Foundation repair is structural, so the Limited program will not cover it. The Standard program requires a HUD consultant, and we coordinate with that consultant, a licensed foundation contractor and, where needed, a structural engineer to scope, price and document the repair so it satisfies both the lender and the city inspector. Leveling is sequenced before finishes so the new drywall does not crack.

faqs.q: Do you work with Houston buyers' agents and loan officers?
faqs.a: Yes. Agents and loan officers often bring us in early to help buyers understand repair costs on a Houston listing before an offer goes in. We provide the detailed bid and schedule the loan requires, coordinate access during the option period, and keep everyone informed as draws are requested, inspected and released. That early look often keeps a buyer from overpaying for a house whose drains or foundation were never going to be cheap.

faqs.q: What if the house is in a floodplain?
faqs.a: The lender will require flood insurance in special flood hazard areas, and a large renovation could trigger City of Houston substantial-improvement rules. We check floodplain status early and explain how it affects the scope and the buyer's costs, so buyers and agents can decide with full information before the appraisal is ordered. Some buyers move on to a house outside the mapped area once they see the full picture.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in Houston, TX | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: Houston REO renovation for servicers, banks and GSEs: flood and mold remediation, freeze damage, vandalism repair and code compliance across Harris County.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovation in Houston
reo-renovation.intro: Bank-owned houses in Houston face a particular set of problems once they sit empty. Without air conditioning running, humidity turns drywall and cabinets into mold farms within a single summer. Freezes like Winter Storm Uri burst pipes in unheated homes. Storms push water through roofs that nobody is watching, and vacant houses attract break-ins and copper theft. Genstone works with mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, which use us as a preferred contractor, to stabilize, repair and prepare REO properties for sale. Genstone Field Services handles property preservation, inspections and code compliance, and our construction team handles renovation. Together we coordinate licensed contractors across Houston, document every step and keep your asset moving toward disposition.

sections.h2: Common conditions in vacant Houston homes
sections.body:
Mold is the most common finding in Houston REO properties. When the power is shut off or the thermostat is set high to save on utilities, humidity climbs and organic growth spreads across walls, ceilings, cabinets and ductwork. Remediation often includes removing affected drywall and insulation, cleaning or replacing ductwork, and drying the structure before rebuilding.

Water damage from roof leaks, burst pipes and street flooding is a close second. Winter Storm Uri left many vacant Houston homes with split supply lines in attics and exterior walls, and some were not discovered until long after the thaw. Vandalism and theft are also common, especially stripped copper, outdoor AC condensers and water heaters, which leave a house without cooling and accelerate the mold problem. Foundation movement can worsen while a house sits empty and the yard goes unwatered through a dry summer. Our initial inspection documents each of these conditions with photos so servicers can make repair or as-is decisions quickly.

REO work in Houston usually happens in three stages. First, stabilization: secure doors and windows, tarp roofs, shut off water if needed, remove debris and trash-outs, and start drying or dehumidification. Genstone Field Services handles much of this through property preservation. Second, repair: address the conditions that affect value or marketability, such as mold remediation, roof replacement, replacing stolen AC equipment and plumbing repairs. Third, preparation for sale: paint, flooring, cleaning and curb appeal work so the listing photographs well.

Our estimators can provide multiple scope options, from a minimal repair for an as-is investor sale to a fuller renovation aimed at owner-occupant buyers using FHA financing. We include dumpster and debris removal in every estimate, which matters on Houston REO homes where trash-outs are often large and may include water-damaged contents. Draws are tied to completed, documented work, and our field managers provide milestone photos so asset managers can follow progress remotely and report it up the chain without sending someone to the property.

Vacant homes in Houston can attract code enforcement attention for overgrown yards, open structures, standing water that breeds mosquitoes and dangerous conditions. The city's Department of Neighborhoods handles many of these complaints, and properties left unaddressed can face citations or dangerous-building proceedings. Genstone Field Services monitors properties, keeps lawns cut through the long growing season and responds to code issues so the asset does not accumulate violations.

When repair work begins, permits go through the Houston Permitting Center, or through Harris County or the relevant suburban city for addresses outside city limits. Flood-damaged properties in mapped floodplains may face substantial-damage determinations, which can decide whether the house can be repaired without being raised. We flag those cases early so servicers can choose between repair, as-is sale or other disposition paths with the facts in hand. Lien waivers and contractor compliance documents are collected for every job, and we keep the documentation package organized for audit.

faqs.q: Do you handle mold remediation on Houston REO properties?
faqs.a: Yes. We coordinate remediation contractors to remove affected materials, treat the structure and dry it properly before rebuilding. Clearance documentation can be provided where the servicer or buyer requires it. We also address the cause, such as a roof leak, a missing condenser or poor humidity control, so the problem does not come back after the house is listed and sits through another humid month.

faqs.q: Can you work across the Houston suburbs for a servicer portfolio?
faqs.a: Yes. Our licensed contractor network covers the Houston metro, including Pasadena, Baytown, Humble, Katy, Pearland, Sugar Land and unincorporated Harris County. Each job gets a field manager and consistent documentation, whatever the jurisdiction, so asset managers see the same reporting format across every address in the pool. Jurisdiction is confirmed per address, since permitting and floodplain review differ between the city, the county and each suburb.

faqs.q: Do you provide as-is and repaired scope options?
faqs.a: Yes. Our estimators can price a minimal repair scope for as-is marketing to investors and a fuller renovation for retail or FHA buyers. That helps servicers compare likely net proceeds and choose the disposition strategy that fits the asset, its flood history and its neighborhood before money is spent. Both options include debris removal, photo documentation and a clear line-item breakdown.
